rename.resolution: Executed 2026-09-03. `try_recv{,_raw,_sequence,_validated}` -> `take{,_serialized,_sequence,_validated}` in C, C++ and Rust; `try_recv_request` -> `take_request`, `try_recv_reply_raw` -> `take_response_raw`. The blocking contract collision was resolved by DELETING `PollingSubscription<M>::take(M&)` (a convenience duplicating `take_data()`, zero real callers) rather than by picking a third word. Re-verdicted to divergence for the residue -- byte-oriented because there is no typesupport dispatch and no allocator.

why:
phase-492 W8: the typed take is `rclc_polling_subscription_take(sub, &msg, NULL)`, deserialising through the descriptor into caller-wired storage. `rcl_take` itself is NOT declared: it takes an `rcl_subscription_t`, which here is executor-owned (phase-487 W1) and has no subscriber of its own to take from, so rcl's name with this contract would compile and differ. A subscription the caller drains is an `rclc_polling_subscription_t`.

History: RE-VERDICTED 2026-09-03 (phase-379 W6 decision 1), rename -> divergence: the WORD moved and what is left has a constraint behind it.
EXECUTED: `try_recv` -> `take` across C, C++ and Rust. Note the direction this went -- our own RMW vtable (`nros/rmw_vtable.h`) has spelled these slots `take` / `take_request` / `take_response` / `take_sequence` since phase-376 W3.b, so the USER API was the only layer still saying `try_recv`; the rename moves it onto the vocabulary the layer beneath it already used, which is also rcl's (`rcl_take`) and rclcpp's (`Subscription::take`). The contract collision that blocked this row is gone too: `PollingSubscription<M>::take(M&)` -- non-consuming, retained-latest, the opposite contract under the same word -- was DELETED, its `take_data()` / `take_new_data()` autoware mirrors (issue 0278) retained. Old C spellings survive as NROS_DEPRECATED_MSG `static inline` forwarders in `rclc/subscription.h`, `rclc/service.h` and `rclc/client.h`; C++ as `[[deprecated]]` methods; Rust took a clean break with no shim, because a rename there breaks IMPLEMENTORS of the RMW traits rather than callers and a compile error is what a backend author wants.
WHAT REMAINS, and the constraint. `rcl_take(subscription, void *ros_message, rmw_message_info_t *, rmw_subscription_allocation_t *)` is ONE type-erased function over typesupport plus an allocator. We have neither on target, so the type-erased take is byte-oriented -- `nros_subscription_take_serialized(subscription, buf, buf_len)` -- and the typed take is generated per message type. That is exactly `c:publish`'s divergence mirrored on the receive side. The `nros_subscription_` prefix is not a second difference: it is a module prefix of the construction rcl itself uses (`rcl_client_fini`), and the precedent chain (`c:get_zero_initialized_publisher`, verdict DECLINED) argues for keeping ours.
